title: Fix Duplicate Header Row In Zwischenbericht Bestand Table
description: In the Zwischenbericht mit Bestand print report, the first data row of a SemioTableThree table (e.g. the Netzwerk/Arbeitspakete table with header "AP / Partner / Schwerpunkt im Berichtszeitraum") visually overlaps with the header row — header cell text and the first body row's text render on overlapping baselines within the same band (e.g. "AP" + "AP-Erfahrung" merge into "APAP-Erfahrung"). Root cause: print/tex/semio-table.sty applies \noalign{\vskip-\topskip} unconditionally right after \hline in both \SemioTableHeaderRow (line ~27) and the long-table repeating header macro \semio@table@long@header@repeat@three (line ~155), pulling the next row up into the header's vertical space. Need to remove/guard this negative skip so header and first body row no longer overlap, without breaking the intended long-table first-page-top compensation (there's already a \ifsemio@table@long@first@row flag that isn't being consulted).
summary:
Fixed the header/first-row overlap in SemioTableThree and long-table headers (e.g. the Zwischenbericht mit Bestand "Netzwerk" Arbeitspakete table). Root cause: print/tex/semio-table.sty applied 
oalign{\vskip-	opskip} right after \hline in \SemioTableHeaderRow and \semio@table@long@header@repeat@three, pulling the following body row up into the header's vertical space (visually merging "AP" + "AP-Erfahrung" into "APAP-Erfahrung"). Attempted moving the negative skip to before the header row instead, but 
oalign is only legal immediately after a \ / \cr, not as the literal first token of a tabular body (confirmed via "Misplaced 
oalign" error in a standalone isolated test) — so the compensation was simply removed from both macros as it served no correct purpose in either position. Also removed the dead, never-consulted \ifsemio@table@long@first@row flag and its three ...true assignments for cleanliness. Verified via a standalone LaTeX doc (kept in this ticket folder) that renders SemioTableThree with a header + 2 body rows: header and first row are now visually distinct with no overlap. Note: the repo-wide print build is currently broken for an unrelated, pre-existing reason — print/tex/semio-core.sty references semio-chrome-light-base/dark-base/etc. theme colors that are never defined anywhere in the repo. This affects all print documents, not just this table, and looks like in-progress work from another concurrent session (sibling open ticket PRINT-HEADER-FOOTER-NAVBAR-SPACING-PARITY touches the same chrome/spacing area). Flagged separately via spawn_task rather than fixed here to avoid colliding with that concurrent work.
